facts.text: Framing: historical retrospective of Italy's 2024 European election, not current voting instructions.
Election dates in Italy: 8 and 9 June 2024; seats to elect: 76 members of the European Parliament.
Voting age minimum: 18 years; election system: proportional representation.
Preference rule: one to three preferences within the same list; with two or three preferences, candidates of different sexes.
National electoral threshold: 4%; constituencies: five, assigned by residence.
Voting is not compulsory; it is a civic duty. Assigned polling station is on the voting card; missing card: contact the municipality.

facts.text: Framing: retrospective of WHO statement dated 14 August 2024; not a claim about present emergency status.

WHO Director-General declared the mpox upsurge in the DRC and a growing number of African countries a public health emergency of international concern under IHR (2005), following independent expert advice.
Further spread across Africa and possibly beyond was a risk, not a certainty.
Second mpox PHEIC in two years; previous declaration: July 2022; ended: May 2023 after sustained global decline.
Initial anticipated response funding requirement: US$15 million; already released from the Contingency Fund for Emergencies: US$1.45 million. Do not swap requested and released amounts.

Vaccine Emergency Use Listing process initiated the previous week to accelerate access where national approval was missing and facilitate procurement by Gavi and UNICEF; not a statement that listing had already completed.

facts.text: Framing: historical account of European Commission announcement on 3 October 2025, not an updated disbursement report.
Disaster: October 2024 floods in Valencia, with more than 230 deaths and extensive infrastructure destruction.
Commission proposed 945 million euros from the EU Solidarity Fund (FSUE) to Parliament and Council; not yet their approval.
Separate measure already approved: reallocation of 645 million euros of cohesion funding through RESTORE; combined headline nearly 1.6 billion euros is not all already paid.
Advance of 100 million euros already paid; remaining FSUE balance payable after Parliament and Council approval, less that advance.
RESTORE permits EU co-financing of up to 95% of eligible costs, not 95% of all losses; progressive payment depends on expenditure.
Supported areas include infrastructure repair, temporary accommodation, cleaning and restarting small and medium-sized businesses.
